longLivedAssets.label: Long-lived assets
longLivedAssets.definition: Long-lived assets by country (10-K Note 13, Segment information), which "exclude goodwill, intangible assets, non-marketable investments and deferred taxes". Each row lists FY2026 revenues then FY2026 long-lived assets first; the long-lived assets value is recorded (revenue is not).

notes: Oracle publishes no state or country economic-impact report that was found, and its FY2026 10-K (year ended May 31, 2026) gives no property or headcount breakdown by state or country beyond the U.S./international employee split (49,000 U.S., 92,000 international of ~141,000 full-time employees) and the long-lived assets by country in its geographic note (U.S., UK, Germany, Japan, other). Item 2 gives the owned Austin HQ (~0.9M sq ft), ~25.4M sq ft of other office facilities "in various other locations in the U.S. and abroad" (about 45% sublet or marketed for sublease), the leased Hillsboro, Oregon hardware plant, and "approximately 181 data center locations globally, substantially all of which are leased" (no locations listed). Oracle's public cloud region list exists on oracle.com but is a list of locations with no figures and was not recorded. The "Outside the U.S." employee region and the "Other countries" long-lived-asset region are different groupings (the latter excludes UK, Germany and Japan).
